title: Releaseflow Anchor: compat migration orchestrator for Private VPC rollouts
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Design and implement a migrator/orchestrator (Releaseflow Anchor) for Redwood Private that coordinates multi-stage upgrades and data/schema migrations across VPC/on-prem fleets. The goal is to provide a safe, observable, and reversible rollout path for LTS channel changes and minor/major releases while minimizing downtime and operational cognitive load for customers running private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can execute a predefined migration plan (phases + per-node steps) and surface progress to Console
Preflight checks validate compatibility matrix and block incompatible nodes; plans fail fast with clear remediation hints
Canary rollout support: run migration on a configurable subset of hosts with automatic health evaluation and automated promotion/rollback
Schema migrations are idempotent and use a two-phase (deploy-compatible, data-migrate) pattern with pause/resume support
Telemetry emits upgrade_success_rate, step_latency_ms, canary_failure_count, and rollback_triggered with tags: cluster, release_channel, plan_id
Operator runbook and Console UI show per-step logs with links to recovery actions
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight Releaseflow Anchor controller that orchestrates existing private agent; controller stores plan state in the local control plane (encrypted) with an append-only event log for audit
Migration model: express plans as ordered steps and checkpoints; steps can be: preflight, drain, apply-binary, apply-config, run-migrations, kv-prefix-rotate, smoke-test
Use a saga-style compensating action library for rollbacks; prefer idempotent compensators where possible
Compatibility gating: integrate with model/serving compatibility matrix service to evaluate runtime and kernel constraints prior to binary rollout
Data path: for KV cache invalidation we will implement a prefix-rotation strategy that avoids full cache flush across the fleet; compatible runtime must support dual-read during transition
For DB schema: use feature-flagged read path first (backwards-compatible columns), then backfill in a controlled batch, then cut over to new read path
Runtime coordination: leverage existing private agent handshake and new "plan-agent" API for step execution and heartbeat; all RPCs are idempotent and traceable
Observability: add tracing hooks in runtime and surface traces in Console trace view; Grafana dashboard: /d/upgrade/Releaseflow-Anchor (prototype: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/upgrade)
Storage: plan state is encrypted at rest using KMS; operators can export audit events for compliance
risks: Network partitions could leave partially-completed migrations; mitigated via step-level idempotency and long-lived leases
Incompatible third-party kernel changes could only be detected during canary and require rollback; keep short canary windows and automated health checks
Large data backfills risk rolling window pressure on throughput; require throttling and dynamic concurrency control
Operator error when creating plans; minimize surface area in Console and provide curated templates for common upgrade types

2026-02-10 - Liam Chen: Spike complete - validated two-phase schema pattern on local cluster. PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/releaseflow/tree/poC-migration
2026-02-15 - Security review (prelim): requested HSM integration for plan signing and KMS-backed plan secrets. Action: schedule sec consult (SEC-2026-018).
2026-02-20 - Design review (PM): Ana Patel approved canary UX flows; asked for explicit operator confirmation step for major release promotions
2026-02-22 - Engineering: added plan-agent API spec to internal API catalog: https://git.internal/redwood/api-specs/plan-agent.yml

2026-02-28 - QA: created end-to-end harness using kinD + local agent; automated smoke tests added to CI (releaseflow-e2e pipeline). Build: https://github.com/redwood-inference/releaseflow/actions/runs/8249123

2026-03-01 - Demo: ran a staged canary against staging-priv cluster (5 hosts). Observations: KV prefix rotation work had a 12s median tail due to keyspace eviction. Follow-up: add staggered rotation windows (ENG-FOLLOWUP-01).
2026-03-03 - PM feedback: require an explicit rollback policy document per plan. Action: add plan-level policy fields (max_retries, rollback_on_failure, notify_slack_channel)
2026-03-04 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/releaseflow/pull/1893 - implements plan state machine and plan-agent handshake. Requesting reviews from @devinfra and @sec-team
2026-03-05 - Observability: prototype dashboard available (internal): https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/upgrade/releaseflow-anchor; key panels: step success rate, live plan heatmap, per-host latency
Next steps: complete KMS integration, add operator-runbook.md to docs, implement plan templating in Console, finalize security sign-off
review_feedback: PM (Ana Patel): prefer conservative defaults - 0.5% canary by default and explicit opt-in to full rollout
Design: add collapseable step detail UI per plan with links to relevant PRs and runbooks
Security: require plan signatures for scheduled automatic rollouts; require audit export within 90 days retention window
Reliability lead (Marco Silva): include automated rate-limit backoff for KV rotation to prevent cascading OOMs
next_steps: Finish KMS/HSM plan-signing integration (blocked on SEC ticket SEC-2026-018)
Add plan templating UI to Console and a curated set of templates for minor and major LTS upgrades
Implement automatic health-evaluator plugin based on existing canary metrics (latency and error-rate heuristics)
Expand e2e tests to cover pause/resume and compensating actions for rollback scenarios
Schedule a security review meeting and request final sign-off
